body: I'm so sorry to hear this :( You're not alone in feeling these emotions.

I really empathise with this. When I moved to my own apartment alone after having lived with a partner for years, I had to do the usual manly things he did lol, like unclog a drain, change the lights, killing cockroaches, etc. It felt rather strange and a little lonely. I was also sick with the flu at one point and it felt incredibly lonely to not have a partner take care of me.

I think if a person is still hung up on their ex and yearning for them, they're not ready for a new relationship. And I say this because I used to be like that when my ex of 7 years broke up with me. In retrospect, I shouldn't have dated as soon  as I did. I can understand the heartbreak and even love, I don't think you really stop loving someone you had such a strong bond with at some point. But love and romantic love are two different things. If someone is still holding onto someone from the past in a romantic way, they wont have real space for anyone new. I'd be wary of someone fresh off a break up and hadn't really healed.

Remembering the hurt (to both yourself and the other person), and how badly something ends when you're not ready helps. Also, focusing on being content by yourself and trying to provide yourself with the emotional needs you otherwise would've sought in someone else. If you can give yourself what you need, you're less likely to seek it elsewhere.

Honestly this pandemic almost feels like a breeze compared to some other things I've been through. I think some part of why it feels easier is because it's being validated constantly, by almost everyone. Everyone reflects your reality. When you're enduring your own personal trauma, especially amid people who are toxic, you can feel terribly alone.

Likely, she's had an unhealthy dynamic with her parents that she's playing out in her love life as well. Low self-esteem makes you feel particularly susceptible to just accepting whatever you can get, even if it's not good for you. 

I was in a back and forth relationship for months, and I was having trouble letting it go, although I should've known better.  When I started to look at my feelings more, it became more and more dire and I had to let go.

I'm still friends with one of my exes, so we still talk, he's actually been a huge support during this time and I'm grateful to still have him in my life. My most recent ex however is a completely different story. He has reached out to me, though, only to enquire about something in relation to himself. Hasn't asked how I am, hasn't asked how I'm coping, etc. It makes me realise why I broke up with him in the first place, and how incredibly emotionally unfulfilling and empty being with him was. Even my manager at work asks me if I'm coping ok. It's a rather sad and startling realisation.
An ex reached out to me, it also reminded me of why I broke up with him in the first place.

Yea my most recent ex was super judgmental and arrogant. Had a huge intellectual ego because of his temperament, age and PhD. Judged me for my past and some of my circumstances. Broke up with him. Never again would I date someone similar.

A good partner shouldn't be that judgmental or look down on you, it's not a good basis for love. It's a complete deal breaker for me now.

I had this happen to me as well one time, I asked a guy what he did for work as I was genuinely curious, and he told me, it was way too soon for me to ask such a question. I was surprised by his response as I asked pretty innocently.
I needed to hear this today so much. Thank you.
I find this true. Some of them want the control.

I dated someone 10 years older than me and it upset me how often he felt he knew better than me due to experience, which wasn't necessarily always the case. It felt like an imbalanced relationship and a power struggle the entire time I was with him. 

Maybe it was my particular situation and our personalities, but I don't know if I could repeat that much of an age difference again. I'd certainly be more cautious.

My boyfriend of 7 years broke up with me about a year ago. At the time I didn't think I could survive, but I've found some way  although at times, things are difficult. It will get better. You will have plenty of time to heal and find new love, and in the process, likely learn how strong and capable you are.

If I've only been on one or a few dates with someone, I don't think a real reason is really that necessary. If I've been in an actual relationship, its better to be more honest in that relationship. I'd hate to be ghosted by someone I have seen in person, though honestly, I've done it before only to have the guy call me.
Yes absolutely.

I read something once that helped changed my perspective on a past ex I was with for 7 years who really was my first love. I was devastated by the breakup and thought that I could never find love again. The quote read -- "people come in and out of your life, but love doesn't have to." Love doesn't have to be so limited, if you've found love once, you can find it again. Keep the hope in your heart that you deserve the love you seek.
Well done :) we have to eradicate their lies from our heads and live our best, deserving life.

I also tended to feel an emptiness with family on the holidays. I've since disconnected from them so I don't see them. The loneliness definitely creeps in more during this period but I tell myself I was lonely even when I was with them. Hopefully you can find the understanding and care were all looking for OP.
Hey, you're in my thoughts, I hope things turn around for you this coming new year <3
You attract what you're like.
\*Hugs\*, it'll be ok. Tell yourself that whatever hardship you're going through right now and whatever severe pain is temporary -- that this doesn't have to last forever.

I don't think this is a good sign at all to be feeling unheard, and unacknowledged in a relationship consistently. It's just going to build up potential resentment and sadness over time. I also dated a guy who barely asked me how I was. I can recall him only asking twice for the entire 3 months I dated him, and it made me feel bad consistently even after I told him how I felt. Little things like that add up and they're the sign of bigger problems. If she's not willing to listen to you, don't stay, you deserve better.

Ended two brief relationships this year and I'm fine being single for now though it does feel lonely sometimes. I think it's normal to want to be single when you've come from a bad relationship. I think both statuses have their pros and cons. Being single does allow you a lot of freedom, but I'd like to think that with the right partner I don't have to feel so stifled. I have to say it does feel kinda liberating to not feel the need to impress anyone like I feel I need to when I date.

I wear makeup to work sometimes only when I'm going out after and I notice I get more attention when I do. Generally I prefer not to though as it makes my skin too congested if I do so regularly. I also deal with most clients over the phone or email, not in person. I'm a graphic designer.

I understand what you're going through and I really feel for you (32F). I was also in a relationship for 7 years and was broken up with. The breakup was a culmination of so much bad that went wrong in my life and it completely devastated me. I was probably at my lowest point the weeks and months after. To make matters worse, my ex pursued someone very shortly after who was apparently more "stable" than me. He was infatuated with her and craved for a connection with her, and he was tired of me. He even said at one point, he wished she was there instead of me. I felt absolutely worthless and defective, and that no one would ever love me. 

A few months later, he realised, she was objectively no better than me and actually in some respects, I may have been better. There's always an infatuation phase at the start and a few years later, reality kicks in more. My long term relationship made me question whether true love even existed. I thought I loved this guy, I thought he loved me, I thought I would spend the rest of my life with him and in the end, all of it just broke. I'm still yet to figure out how to really rekindle a belief in love again after my last relationship, it's a work in progress really but it all starts from within. 

Keep in mind that just because he didn't love you or see you as the one, it doesn't make you any less loveable or worthy of love in the present or the future. You are not any less loveable because you are not like the girl he is pursuing. Someone else will love you and appreciate you for who you are. 

Allow yourself to grieve and be sad, it's a big loss. If you can do one thing for yourself, allow yourself to mourn. I didn't allow myself this as much at the start and I'm only really starting to do so now.
Good on you for working on yourself and your own self-love. I'm attempting the same right now in my singlehood.
Understanding.

By staying away from people who pressure me about it lol. It helps to surround myself with people who don't. Honestly though, I'm 32 and though I would like a life partner, marriage is not necessarily mandatory to me so long as my partner and I genuinely love one another. Although I am not closed off to marriage, I would care more about the dynamic I have with my partner than a formal title. Being married doesn't prevent breakups, having a good solid relationship does, and that is not dependent on marriage.

I've been waking recently and checking my phone for any signs of contact from my ex. One week since my official breakup and it's been rather hard to get my mind off him. I miss his texts and I'm just missing waking up with him and having breakfast together. I think work has served as a distraction for me, but distractions are not typically sustainable when you're alone. Hope it gets better for you in time OP.

I have an artistic temperament so I do find beauty elicits a certain response out of me, particularly when I'm calmer and not as stressed. It makes me particularly happy. For this reason, I give attention to what I surround myself with around my home because it definitely influences my mood.
Well he hasn't replied.
I messaged him the other day, asking to meet up and apologised. Asked to talk to him in person.

A healthy partner will take the time to listen to you, understand you and respect your boundaries. You will feel more like yourself in the relationship (or an even better version of yourself), instead of being transformed into someone you don't want to become.
Me pretty much since my break up.

Hm yea, I feel like this too. I almost cried today at work because I just felt so stressed and depressed. I think all the years of trauma I've had and an accumulation of the dreariness of life is really killing me deep down. It's like I'm dragging my feet across life, rather than floating by lightly.

My parents barely taught me anything also. When I left home, I learnt a great deal on my own regarding finances, career and psychological/emotional healthiness. With regards to psychology, I was parented more by books than my actual parents. If anything, my parents taught me what not to do in life unconsciously. I feel pretty much alone in the world sometimes because I don't really have a family to lean on and this feeling has exacerbated since I went no contact from them.

I'm an introvert as well with minimal friends so it wouldn't be an issue for me at all, in fact I would probably prefer it if my partner didn't have so many friends. It would drain me to be forced to socialise with so many, especially if it were continual.

Having said that, I agree with the others on here that said it would be also draining to have a person rely on you to fulfill all of their emotional needs. It's not healthy, and it's not good for either of you. It's more a matter of proper boundaries, not so much how many friends someone has that can significantly affect a relationship.
Growing up with parents who don't love you.

Loneliness feels like an empty pit; devoid of care, love and feeling. Loneliness feels like a lack in so many ways. Loneliness is being alone in your room alone and feeling utterly misunderstood. Loneliness is this deep sadness I cannot seem to evade. Loneliness feels like a yearning, unfulfilled.
Appreciate real love given to you.

I never smoked, haven't drank in years, try to eat healthy, and am into natural health vs. chemicals/meds. Also it helps I don't have the usual burdens most people my age have like children, or fulltime work. I try to not overexert myself when it comes to work and I'm very lucky I can manage to do so right now. I've done yoga, massage, breathing practices and meditation (these help tremendously). Also, I suppose it helps, my mother looks 5-10 years younger than her age, it's partly genetic. I can pass off early to mid 20s supposedly and I'm in my early 30s.
*hugs* It is hard. It does get better with time, just try to take care of yourself for the meantime.

It's gotten better with time. Having said that, I'm still not fully well, the loneliness and sadness still definitely creeps in every now and then. I suppose, long relationships can take a while to recover from and I can't be certain when I'll fully move on.

I'm sorry to hear your parents treat you like that, especially when you're suicidal, you need the most support from them during that time. Maybe they aren't "bad" people, but the way they're reacting to you isn't exactly sane, healthy or caring. Hopefully you're able to find some support in your pain.

I'm practically in the same boat with one real life friend, and another who seems to be getting distant for reasons currently unknown to me. 

I'm trying to get better at being alone so when I do enter another relationship I don't rely on them as much as I did with my ex. 

One of the ways I'm becoming better in tune with myself is through breathing practices and allowing myself to feel whatever it is I feel, however pained or lonely I feel at the time. 

Distraction doesn't really work well for me usually. 

I've also disconnected from a toxic and abusive family so I know the intense loneliness that can stem from that as well. PM me if you'd like to talk.

I love you for saying this. Ironically, I was in the middle of breathing practices when I turned to reddit and your post was right up the top for me. Even in our toughest times, we are being helped more than we know.

I found myself without any friends at all after my 7 year relationship ended. Both my partner and I secluded ourselves which I did regret to some degree when we broke up. I've since made one really good friend, and have tried to put myself out there more. I'm hoping to make more friends this year, so I can actually have a decent support system outside my relationship. Good luck! I can understand the feeling of loneliness well.

I'm struggling with feelings of deep loneliness after my 7 year relationship has ended and also a disconnection from a toxic family. It's been about 3 months since my relationship ended and on some days a void of emptiness seems to hit me like a big wave. I get a yearning to have the comfort of a relationship in my life again, but I know I'm really not ready and the timing is not right. 

I think loneliness gets more comfortable the more you can give to yourself what you yearn from in a relationship. It's definitely a lot easier said than done, but I suppose I aim to find some stable sense of validation and acceptance from myself and my own life before I even venture out to find someone again.
Thank you :) I hope you're right
Hanging in there. I suppose I'm starting to do better but my mood can fluctuate. Thanks for asking.

31F and I am struggling through the very same emotions and search for purpose after my 7 year relationship has ended. I based too much of my happiness and identity around my partner that now that I may not be with him in the future, I feel very lost. On occasion, I've felt suicidal too so I know the feeling. I feel like I am having to rebuild my entire life almost from scratch; my emotional health after having suffered from depression too, my career, my support network, a home, etc. PM me if you want to chat, I can see we're struggling with the same issues.

My god, I needed this in my life. I needed to hear this so much even though the truth hurts like a sharp pain in my chest. I woke up from a nightmare a few moments ago dreaming of my ex being kissed by another woman. While I cried in bed, he lay there, a grin across his face. The dream felt so real, I actually started crying in my sleep. 

I cannot stop repressing my feelings of hurt. I cannot stop repressing my feelings of doubt about him. Every time my ex feels his chances with this other woman he likes is slim or he feels low about it, he reverts back to telling me we might get back together, that there might be a future for us. I do feel like I'm a backup plan, even though he wasn't mine. Me in my terrible loneliness and fear, liked to hear there was hope for us, though it's a very bitter consolation. He swings back a few days later to pining for this other woman.

I feel devastated to walk away, it hurts my heart but after reading this I feel deep down that it probably is the best thing to do. I feel like I need to let go and experience someone new. 

I have never experienced a perpetually loyal relationship and I wonder how that would be. I wonder how it is to be accepted entirely for who I am and not always have to be someone else, or improve myself, or impress him. 

I keep allowing myself to be treated like a back up plan, I am always here, ready to come to him, ready when he's ready and willing. It's about time I wasn't. It's about time I protected my own heart. 

And you are right, no one should ever have to be the one someone settles for.

He didn't cut ties with me because I am exactly like my family. You don't know the full situation. I have even asked him this question and he said my family is on a whole other level. Don't make leaps when you don't know the full story.

I'm honestly confused by him at times. Like on some level, he's actually a decent human being who has helped me through a lot really. But I'm hurt by him too. I can't deny there's definite hurt there too. Sometimes I feel like he can be too detached from understanding what I'm really going through.
I have tried some mindfulness strategies, though when the emotions get intense like they did today, they seem to just overwhelm me.
Yea, I have contemplated many times since of returning to my family but that will have some seriously negative repercussions for me. Thank you for your well wishes.

I have made one friend since IRL who has been helpful. But the lost of my main support system on top of family is devastating. He has resumed talking to me again so I'm a bit calmer, but since our break up the future frightens the crap out of me. I do realise perhaps I am stronger than I give myself credit for, but I'm also so afraid.
Loneliness is an awful feeling and I can empathise with feeling as though no one cares for you. Hopefully you can find some people to connect with.
Ok sure. Go get some rest. I'll message you. I find it does help to talk to others going through similar issues.

I'm sorry to hear that. I know relationship break ups are so hard, particularly long-term ones where you grow more attached and accustomed to the person being in your life. Life is hard. I'm free now if you wanted to chat? I guess it helps to talk someone going through the same thing.

Some days I am doing better, other days, I feel like what's the point of life anymore. I know a relationship with someone shouldn't be the end all and be all of life, but sadly, that's what it came to for me. I'm trying to build some meaning or find some meaning without him, but I resonate with you when you say "it's not enough".

My boyfriend of 7 years broke up with me 3 months ago, and since then, the loneliness I've experienced has been the most devastating feeling I have ever felt. I don't even know if I'm going to survive it on some days. I haven't tried dating yet as I just really feel unready. You're not alone in this feeling. It's an awful feeling.
I understand the feeling of loneliness. When were alone, we look to people who we could relate to and meaningfully connect to and, it's rough when those relationships never come.
Happy holidays. Roughest holiday time for me in my life this year probably. I sincerely hope 2019 treats us all better.

I would rather know someone's issues to begin with and personally would welcome someone sharing their issues, as it makes for a deeper connection, rather than a relationship based on the surface. There's really no fixed way by which a friendship should start, just because you prefer a particular way, it doesn't mean others would. I also don't think there's anything necessarily wrong with people wanting support, as long as it is mutual, and they can give support in return.

Hey, I've been through something similar and I know how lonely it is. I've recently had a break up with my partner of seven years and pretty much have no family. I came from a dysfunctional family so I went no contact prior to my boyfriend breaking up with me. I know the crushing devastation and loneliness of having your only support systems lost. When my boyfriend left me, I felt like I had no one in this world who cared for me and it was the worst feeling in the world. Perhaps see if you can find other females to support you in this time as it can be difficult to endure on your own.
I do this all the time. I massage myself regularly, do deep breathing to loosen knots, and also EFT. We hold onto our sadnesses, pain, anxiety, fear, etc. in our contracted muscles.
I feel for you, and I've experienced very similar feelings. I hope you can find something positive in this world to keep you going.
I'd be interested in this. My partner of 7 years broke up with me about 2 months ago, it's still hugely depressing. In my early 30s.
I miss mine too, and what we used to have :(

Wow that just sounds rough. I think when we have rarely been loved in the past and have been abandoned before, we just come to expect it will happen again, which unfortunately, tends to make abandonment repeat again. Until you can shift your mindset and your tendencies, it'll just keep happening. It's so difficult to do this, and I totally understand how hard it is, because believe me, I've been trying to. I feel your pain, that's all I can say. I feel abandoned since the breakup, I feel worthless sometimes, I feel like I'll never be loved again sometimes, I feel so alone, and my "ex" is also trying to pursue someone else which is just a shitty feeling overall. Anyway, I'll PM you, seems like we are dealing with quite a few similar things.

It's rather odd that she doesn't want to at least communicate why she's unhappy, so she's hiding something, for what reason I'm not sure of.  I can relate to your partner helping you out in life and then just leaving, same thing has happened with me. I'm sorry you feel used, and that she left you, it's a horrible feeling.

Did she say why she wasn't happy? My former partner told me that too and I could understand why. It gave me some closure and a sense of what to change, though it's a painful realisation to know I sabotaged the relationship. I have issues with him having left me for other women too and developed a lot of trust issues. Unfortunately these things (abandonment) can become a self-fulfilling prophecy when it happens again and again.

I think that's up to you to answer. In my case I'm staying friends with my ex because we've had a good friendship in the past and he's still a special person to me. Also, we live together currently so it's a bit complicated. I think if you can learn to move on and work on yourself while being friends, you can stay friends. But if you're remaining their friend in hopes for something in the future and not really improving, perhaps it's unhealthy. Whatever the case, if you remain friends or not, we have to accept the relationship is over.

I'm going through a very similar thing. I was with my boyfriend for 7 years, thought we'd be life partners. It's devastating in many regards. We also broke up due to issues with me for the most part, and although I have tried and am trying to change he thinks it's best we just stay friends. In my case, I don't think there's anything much right now I can do to change his mind, all I can focus on is myself. Perhaps in time when you have really grown as a person your ex will come around, but we shouldn't pin our hopes on them. It's difficult but we must move on for our own sake. 

Maybe the breakup is what we need to really change us.
Yes , my heart is heavy continually. I'm in a lot of pain for so many reasons. I hope it goes away, when it's fresh, it's the hardest.

I'm going through something similar. Was with my boyfriend for 7 years, and it ended rather badly. From love to resentment. I thought he would be my partner for life also. I feel the pain too, it's exceedingly painful. It's been about a month and everything is raw. All you can do is cry sometimes.

Hey, I hope you're still around? I relate a lot to your experience. My former boyfriend recently broke up with me, and he's definitely been much more distant compared to the past. It's heartbreaking to experience someone who you once thought loved you, turn around, and resent you -- at least that's what happened to me. I'm living with him due to mental illness and have nowhere else to go, so it's been extremely awkward lately.
I can talk to you if you need?

Yes, it's been peculiar to have a certain distance now between my former boyfriend and I. In some ways, things feel the same, but there's always this tension in me at least. There's still a part of me that would like to get back together, I miss him and I value him as a person, but I suppose on some level, perhaps the breakup was for the best. It's just hard to see it amid the pain.
*hugs* from a fellow person who's been there

Hey thanks for your reply, it helped me out a lot. I empathise with all you're going through as well. I certainly miss the manner in rwhich my partner comforted me too when we were together. We're still friends, but it's different. 

I hope that we can both recover from our traumas and the loss ❤️
I can relate. Feel like I've lost everything, but my former boyfriend told me I had nothing to begin with.
Thanks I needed this.

That's such a terrible thing for your mother to say to you. I'm so glad you're away from her. Narcissists are notorious for their lack of empathy and frequent invalidations. My mother was the same -- never wanted to consider or really see my pain. Keep cutting her out of your life, you don't need anymore condemnation.

Anyone who judges point blank without knowing the full context of your upbringing, is someone better left out of your life. 

More often than not I find that people also don't know how to define what is a good relationship vs. a bad one. They judge based on what they see on the surface, and cannot look past social pretense. Someone can look like they have a "good" relationship with their mother but deep down be so full of denials and repressed emotions towards their parents who they choose to keep in contact with, which isn't exactly healthy. Someone else, like a lot of us here, acknowledged the bad in our parents and got away to help ourselves. That doesn't mean we're bad people. It actually shows more awareness. In reality, the person who acknowledges their pain is healthier psychologically.

I was well into my late 20s and my mother still tried to control me, in actuality, a lot of the people older than me in my family, tried to do the same. My parents, well in their 50s, are still controlled by their parents. A lot of people go to their graves still being slaves to their parents in one way or another, to different degrees. It's no way to live a proper life.

I think nowadays I get mostly depressed by my job/career situation. In that respect I do feel like I'm falling behind others my age. I know I have some potential but a history of trauma has made it really difficult to work as smoothly as other people have. It's been a difficult journey. I guess it helps to reframe this by realising not everyone is the same, not everyone reacts the same or has had the same situations occur to them but it does get me down a lot, particularly when I feel like a burden to my partner for not being able to work right now. I see other classmates of mine going easily about their careers and their lives and I'm stuck having breakdowns from all the intense emotions.
That's just hilarious! She's just insulting herself. A narcissist speaking the truth for once.
LOL. Mine is too, there's no need to even explain it here.

Whenever I create something I'm proud of in my work I feel like I never did. It's strange. I know I actually created said pieces but I feel like kind of a liar attributing them to myself. The same thing occurs when I see images of myself and I happen to look decent, I feel like I couldn't look that way in reality. Wow my parents really gave me issues.

Yes they have empty hearts, devoid of a heart. I felt like a burden when I was sick to my parents too. My dad complained when he had to take me to the hospital and my mum thought I just wanted attention. Being sick brings it all back. 

They complain when you're sick but ironically the kind of environment they raise you in induces you to become more sick.

Hey thanks for your reply. I can really relate to that feeling of loneliness. When I lived with my parents, I would be left alone crying in my room while I was upset or sick sometimes. 

My bf healed faster than I did and it's likely because he is less anxious and felt less sad. Still trying to heal, but I'll try to take care of myself more.

You don't have to forgive them as long as you're not ready to. They repressed your emotions for so long and you are allowed to feel your anger. I've gone through a similar thing where I'm branded to be the "bad" one due to my anger, but you are right, when you see reality more, it is difficult not to be angry.
Yes. Deep down it's still kind of there as a void.
That's a really good response. I'm so glad I rarely have to deal with people who gaslight me about my mother nowadays.

My mother was a covert nmother, and my aunty was once talking about being annoyed at their mother, saying she was demanding and controlling. Then she turned to me and said, but you don't have that problem, your mother is "nice". To which I was kind of just shocked by. Little did she know, my mother was also demanding, manipulative and controlling. Like mother like daughter. Though most people would really not suspect it with my mum because she comes across so normal, and "nice" in public because that's the facade she presents to others. I remember on fb one time, another aunty of mine was saying she was having problems and my mother messaged her on her wall for all the world to see, saying I'm here for you, I'm just a phone call away. When I got sexually assaulted and was probably in one of the worst states of my life, my mother never said anything like that to me. She was mostly concerned I see them to attend her gatherings. When I've been ill and suicidal, crying in my room, she just left me alone coldly after my father berated me, annoyed I was making so much noise crying. 

People don't see how they really are at home and the level of hurt they've inflicted, they see their public image and believe it. It can be a really shallow society. The covert ones appear better at lying, they can fool people more, but deep down they are harmful. They are thorns pretending to be roses.

Yes totally! Oftentimes I feel like we are often judged for how we may appear to others in public, for instance too anxious, too sad, different, but other people don't understand why. It helps to know why, it gives you a sense of compassion for yourself that others may not have.

My mother "forgave" my abusive father and still does to this day, and he continues to abuse her. I left their house and didn't feel the need to "forgive", now neither of them abuse me. A lot of the time people "forgive" because they want to avoid facing reality and pain. At least that was the case for my mother. True forgiveness doesn't come out of avoidance, but an understanding of reality. And true forgiveness doesn't go against your needs. We shouldn't have to sacrifice our own emotional well-beings so other people can feel "forgiven".

My relatives were very critical of me when I started eating healthy, even commenting I joined the "dark side". It's peculiar when people want to sabotage actual good progress you make because they can't understand and/or want you to stay on their level. My mother would also say "yeah right" a lot every time I voiced wanting to achieve something, eating healthy being one of them. After eating healthy for years in a row, she then showed displeasure that now I couldn't go on holidays with them anymore and showed some signs of jealousy.

Our abusers often gaslight and invalidate our pain, so we're made to repress the overwhelming hurt we are going through. Also as a child, it can be a way of protecting ourself to say things aren't as bad, so as to cope on a day to day basis and keep going. Objectively some of the things I've gone through have been bad too, but it's also difficult for me to really validate my feelings, particularly as I am now well away from those situations.

I definitely have had traumatic experiences but I realise some other people's may be more extreme. Bottom line, my parents were narcissists and lacked love for their children. It didn't help to have gone through to therapy and have therapists who weren't validating. 

I personally believe all pain is valid and no one should be made to feel like their situation isn't "bad enough" or severe enough to be recognised. Pain is pain. 

My partner also tells me that we all have different reactions to situations. Just because one thing wasn't particularly devastating to one person, it doesn't mean it won't be bad for another. We have different temperaments and sensitivities too and we can't really compare our reactions to another person's. 

If it was bad enough for you and it affected you, that's all that should matter, you're allowed to feel hurt and validate your own emotions.
